newsitem.title: GERMANY: German embassy in Central African Republic to shut.
newsitem.headline: German embassy in Central African Republic to shut.

text.p: Germany said on Thursday it was temporarily closing its embassy in the Central African Republic in the wake of recent clashes between African peacekeepers and army mutineers which killed at least 80 people.
"The situation has already escalated so much that I have decided to temporarily close the German embassy in Bangui," Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said in a statement.
Fighting erupted last week between the disaffected soldiers and the peacekeepers, deployed to the Central African Republic to help restore peace after three army mutinies in under a year.
Witnesses said the two sides had clashed again on Thursday, exchanging automatic fire in Bangui.
Kinkel said he was deeply concerned about developments in several other countries in the region, including Rwanda, Congo and the Democratic Republic of Congo.
"The situation in the heart of Africa must not become the African version of the domino theory," he said.

A spokesman for the Foreign Ministry was unable to say how many staff worked in the Bangui embassy but said the number was small. Germany's embassies in Sierra Leone, Liberia and Congo were also closed at the moment, he said.
Kinkel said the international community had to show a stronger commitment in its African policies to establish the foundations for peace, stability and economic development.
He said the world's leading industrialised nations and Russia had made clear at their summit in Denver last week that it was time Africa made a break from its troubled past.
"We must all help so that the vicious circle of the old mistakes is broken once and for all," he said.
